repair_A2.P1_anytls_vmess_udp_dialer_proxy: AnytlsUot and VmessUdp now receive the same `chain_for` hops as the TCP path and build the server connection through `server_stream` (direct for 1 hop, one socks5 tunnel for 2). Regression: `chained_anytls_udp_with_a_dead_hop_never_reaches_the_echo` and `chained_vmess_udp_with_a_dead_hop_never_reaches_the_echo`; a forced-bypass mutation made the anytls case fail by reaching the echo.
repair_A2.P1_per_destination_associations: anytls UoT, ss UoT (v1/v2) and vmess plain command-2 are no longer bound to the first destination. The relay keeps `HashMap<(proxy, target), writer>` plus one reader task per association (mpsc back to the relay), aborts readers with the association, and retires a writer after a failed write. Regression: the three `*_reaches_two_destinations_from_one_association` cases; a constant-key mutation made the anytls case fail.
repair_A2.P2_anytls_pool: A background ticker now sweeps idle sessions every `idle-session-check-interval` (started on the first pooled session, aborted and idle sessions closed on pool drop); intervals/timeouts `<= 5s` normalize to 30s like `session.NewClient`. Lazy sweep on acquire/release remains as a fallback outside a runtime.
repair_A2.P2_anytls_waker: `AnytlsStream::poll_read` re-checks the inbox and close state after publishing its waker, so a frame queued in that window cannot be lost.
repair_A2.P2_client_fingerprint: Kept as a documented rustls approximation and moved out of `implemented_and_verified` into `approximations_counted_as_residual` (4 matrix rows + the TLS note), with the matrix counts unchanged.
repair_A2.P2_dns_test_race: The dns test fixtures now reserve their TCP/UDP ephemeral ports (`common::bind_loopback{,_udp}`), so a parallel `free_port` cannot hand the UDP port to a fixed `dns.listen`; the dns suite passed 12 consecutive runs.

limitations: uTLS client-fingerprint (vless/anytls/vmess/hysteria2, 4 matrix rows + the shared TLS note): rustls cannot emit a uTLS ClientHello; known pinned names are validated and applied as the closest rustls profile (browser key-exchange list). Extension order/GREASE/cipher list are not reproduced, so these are approximations counted as residuals, not parity.
anytls shadow-tls-opts/jls-opts need a client-controlled ClientHello session id / ServerHello random; rustls exposes neither, so non-empty blocks stay named rejections.
vmess mkcp/mekya/tlsmirror are separate transports (KCP/mekya session/TLS mirror) and remain named rejections.

hysteria2 port hopping/Salamander+Gecko obfs/Brutal up/realm/udp-mtu/bbr-profile require the pinned packet-connection layer and senders quinn does not expose (and the engine has no Hysteria2 UDP relay); they remain named rejections with the reason.

AnyTLS session reuse now has the pinned interval ticker; the ticker is started lazily on the first pooled session (configuration parsing may run outside a runtime) and the lazy acquire/release sweep remains as a fallback.
